financials_interim.notes: INSURER field mapping (general insurer, single-entity filing -- no separate Group/Company columns anywhere in this filing; People's Insurance PLC has no subsidiaries, so this is stored as one GROUP-basis row per this project's single-entity-filer convention, consistent with FCT/JINS precedent). Uses the SIX-MONTH cumulative 'For the six months ended' column on the face Statement of Profit or Loss (p.3), not the 'For the three months ended' Q2-only column also disclosed alongside it. revenue = the filing's own Note 7 'Revenue' subtotal (3,747,220,198) = Net earned premium (3,129,199,516, itself Gross earned premium 4,544,178,236 less Premium ceded to reinsurers net of UPR movement) + Fee income (114,183,020, included within the P&L above Net earned premium but not in Note 7's own build -- see reconciliation note below) + Total other revenue (618,020,682, Note 9: Net interest and dividend income 550,516,641 + Net fair value gains 66,067,355 + Other income 1,436,686) -- this matches the task's prescribed 'Net Earned Premium + Investment/Other Income' concept using the insurer's own disclosed 'Revenue' line (Note 7), which nets to Net earned premium 3,129,199,516 + Total other revenue 618,020,682 = 3,747,220,198 exactly; fee income is already embedded in Net earned premium's presentation path to the Revenue note total, not double-counted. GWP itself (Rs.5,207,840,645, +39% YoY) is the more conventional insurer top-line, cited in the filing's own Financial Review as the headline growth number, but is NOT stored as 'revenue' to stay faithful to the filing's own Note 7 'Revenue' framing (consistent with the JINS precedent of using the insurer's own Net Income/Revenue subtotal rather than GWP). operating_profit = 'Underwriting results' (-92,441,945; H1 2025: -231,902,529) -- UNLIKE AAIC/JINS, this filing DOES disclose a distinct pre-investment-income subtotal on the face P&L (Net earned premium + Fee income - Net claims - Underwriting/acquisition costs - Other operating & admin expenses - Finance cost = Underwriting results), so it is populated here rather than left blank; this is an underwriting-level result BEFORE investment/other income is added, not comparable to a general company's pre-finance-cost operating profit (finance cost of 18,788,070 for H1 2026 is already netted into this figure, per the face P&L). finance_costs = the filing's own separately-itemised 'Finance cost' line (18,788,070; H1 2025: 36,182,628) -- per the cash flow statement's note A this is entirely 'Interest paid on lease liability', i.e. IFRS16 lease interest, not conventional debt interest (the Company has no interest-bearing loans). finance_income left blank: investment income (Note 9, Net interest and dividend income 550,516,641) is presented as part of 'Total other revenue' within the Revenue note, not as a distinct non-insurance finance-income line -- consistent with the AAIC/JINS precedent. gross_profit/cost_of_sales left blank (no COGS concept for an insurer). minority_interest left blank (single entity, no NCI). tax_expense = 168,303,302 (H1 2025: 99,980,820); profit_before_tax = 525,578,737 (H1 2025: 321,565,472); profit_after_tax = 357,275,435 (H1 2025: 221,584,652); identity check ties exactly (525,578,737 - 168,303,302 = 357,275,435). eps_basic = 1.75 (Note 11; H1 2025: 1.09); eps_diluted set equal to eps_basic (only one EPS line disclosed, no separate diluted figure, per the FCT precedent for single-EPS filings) -- cross-check: 357,275,435 / 203,632,478 weighted avg shares = 1.7544, rounds to the printed 1.75, ties. shares_in_issue = 203,632,478 (Note 21, Stated capital note; matches Note 11's weighted average share count exactly, i.e. no share issuance during the period). BALANCE SHEET (as at 30.06.2026): liquidity-ordered Statement of Financial Position (no current/non-current split), so current_assets/current_liabilities are left blank, matching AAIC/JINS precedent. inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per the task's insurer guidance: the closest analogues are Insurance receivables (1,439,818,868 net of a 38,600,744 ECL allowance, Note 13) and Reinsurance receivables (1,266,982,687) on the asset side, and Reinsurance payables (690,478,991) and Other liabilities (1,456,298,164) on the liability side -- all insurance-specific items, not generic trade receivables/payables, and are therefore excluded from those fields rather than force-mapped. Insurance contract liabilities (6,321,807,820, Note 14: net unearned premium 3,787,913,866 + gross outstanding claims 1,654,213,065 + IBNR 879,680,889) are correctly excluded from trade_payables. cash_and_equivalents = balance sheet 'Cash and cash equivalents' asset line (175,408,131); the cash flow statement's own note B nets this against a bank overdraft to a narrower 'cash and cash equivalents at end of period' figure of 138,276,351 used only for the cash-flow reconciliation, not stored here. short_term_borrowings = 'Bank overdrafts' (282,959,463, the only short-term-debt-like line disclosed), consistent with the GLAS/JINS precedent of using the overdraft balance when no dedicated short-term-borrowings line exists. long_term_borrowings = 'Lease liability' (164,654,864) -- there is NO conventional interest-bearing loans line anywhere on this balance sheet (unlike GLAS/LLUB/PKME, where a labelled 'loans and borrowings' line exists and is nil, so lease liabilities are left out); here, lease liability is the ONLY interest-bearing-style obligation disclosed (it carries the 18,788,070 finance cost above), so it is mapped to long_term_borrowings per the GRAN precedent for single-obligation lease-only balance sheets, not split into current/non-current since the SOFP presents it as one unclassified line. total_assets = 15,698,635,075; total_liabilities = 9,369,861,163; total_equity = 6,328,773,912; identity check ties exactly (9,369,861,163 + 6,328,773,912 = 15,698,635,075). CASH FLOW: statement is presented on a clean SIX-MONTH cumulative basis matching the P&L period exactly (no quarterly-only cash flow disclosed, so no YTD/quarterly ambiguity). cash_from_operations = 800,645,861 (Net cash flows from/(used in) operating activities, i.e. the final total after gratuity paid, income tax paid and lease interest paid -- H1 2025: 736,562,459). capex = -15,979,347 (Purchase of property, plant and equipment; the only capex-type line this period, no intangible asset additions disclosed) -- NOTE this does NOT tie to cash_from_investing because the investing section is dominated by financial-investment purchases/sales (Rs.12,488.6mn purchased, Rs.11,591.1mn+Rs.6,069.6mn sold across liquid/other investments), which are the insurer's core investment-book turnover, not capex. cash_from_investing = -736,548,794 (Net cash flows from/(used in) investing activities, the filing's own total, H1 2025: -855,906,548). cash_from_financing = -53,048,158 (Net cash flows from/(used in) financing activities -- entirely lease-liability payments this period, no loan drawdowns/repayments; H1 2025: -16,589,394). Identity checks: PBT-tax=PAT ties exactly for both periods; total_assets=total_liabilities+total_equity ties exactly; EPS ties to PAT/weighted avg shares exactly. No extraction ambiguity encountered in this filing -- single clean column set, no Group/Company duplication.

interim_updates.note_text: People's Insurance (PINS) grew profit 61% in H1 2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026): Profit Before Tax +63% to Rs.525.6mn (Rs.321.6mn), PAT +61% to Rs.357.3mn (Rs.221.6mn), EPS Rs.1.75 vs Rs.1.09; the second quarter alone was stronger still (PBT +120% to Rs.295.1mn, PAT +124% to Rs.200.9mn, EPS Rs.0.99 vs Rs.0.44). Gross Written Premium rose 39% to Rs.5,207.8mn and Net Earned Premium 43% to Rs.3,129.2mn. The growth is concentrated: Motor GWP +39% to Rs.4,047.2mn (78% of the book) and Miscellaneous GWP +78% to Rs.488.3mn (Rs.274.1mn), while Fire grew 23% to Rs.659.0mn and Marine shrank 63% to just Rs.13.3mn. Rs.2,123.8mn of premium (about 41% of GWP) was 'customers introduced' by parent People's Leasing & Finance (up from Rs.1,425.6mn), and a further Rs.84.5mn came via People's Bank -- distribution is heavily dependent on the parent group. Underwriting loss narrowed 60% to Rs.92.4mn from Rs.231.9mn: the pre-overhead underwriting margin rose 30% to Rs.1,035.8mn (Motor Rs.663.5mn, Fire Rs.147.0mn, Miscellaneous Rs.223.5mn, Marine Rs.1.8mn vs Rs.19.0mn), and Other Operating & Administrative Expenses grew only 12% to Rs.1,109.5mn against NEP +43%, i.e. operating leverage rather than better claims. Claims actually worsened in ratio terms: Net Claims +49% to Rs.2,050.1mn (65.5% of NEP vs 62.6%), with Motor claims +52% to Rs.1,946.5mn (71.8% of Motor NEP vs 68.3%); Underwriting & Net Acquisition Costs +76% to Rs.157.4mn and Finance Cost (lease interest) -48% to Rs.18.8mn. Fee income +71% to Rs.114.2mn. Investment and other revenue added Rs.618.0mn (+12%): net interest and dividend income +7% to Rs.550.5mn and net fair-value gains +82% to Rs.66.1mn -- so the investment book still produces more than the entire PBT (Rs.618.0mn vs Rs.525.6mn), meaning underwriting remains loss-making. Income tax rose 68% to Rs.168.3mn (effective rate 32.0% vs 31.1%). Balance sheet: total assets flat at Rs.15.70bn; financial investments +7% to Rs.12.30bn; insurance contract liabilities down 11% to Rs.6.32bn because outstanding claims reserves fell 38% to Rs.1.65bn (claims paid Rs.2,960.8mn vs Rs.1,613.1mn) while the unearned premium reserve grew 10% to Rs.3.79bn; insurance receivables fell 18% to Rs.1.44bn and reinsurance receivables 29% to Rs.1.27bn; operating cash flow Rs.800.6mn (Rs.736.6mn). Equity Rs.6,328.8mn (+6% vs Dec 2025); NAV/share Rs.31.08 (Rs.28.69) versus a last traded price of Rs.28.50, i.e. ~0.92x book. Flags: (1) the quarter is prepared under SLFRS 4 using the SoAT relief for SLFRS 17 -- provisional SLFRS 17 numbers arrive in Q3 and 2025 comparatives will be restated, so later periods will not be like-for-like; (2) tax assessments totalling Rs.350.9mn (Rs.223.1mn tax + Rs.127.8mn penalty, mostly VAT on financial services) are unprovided and under appeal. People's Leasing & Finance holds 75.00%; Fitch A(lka)/Stable.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no predecessor (Q1 2026) row is stored for PINS. Figures are the SIX-MONTH cumulative column compared with H1 2025; the filing's own three-month Q2 columns are cited only where stated. Comparatives are on an SLFRS 4 basis and will be restated for SLFRS 17 in the 2026 annual accounts. The financial review's claim of a 'Rs.2,050.14mn claims cost for the second quarter' actually matches the six-month net claims figure, not Q2 alone (Q2 net claims were Rs.1,064.8mn).
interim_updates.takeaway: A strong top-line and profit quarter driven by motor and miscellaneous growth plus expense leverage, but underwriting is still loss-making (-Rs.92.4mn), claims ratios worsened (65.5% of NEP vs 62.6%) and profit depends on Rs.618.0mn of investment income. Premium sourcing leans on the People's Leasing/People's Bank group (~41% of GWP), and the SLFRS 17 switch in Q3 will reset comparability.
operational_highlights: PBT +63% to Rs.525.6mn, PAT +61% to Rs.357.3mn, EPS Rs.1.75 vs Rs.1.09; Q2 alone PBT +120% to Rs.295.1mn, PAT +124% to Rs.200.9mn
GWP +39% to Rs.5,207.8mn: Motor +39% to Rs.4,047.2mn (78% of book), Miscellaneous +78% to Rs.488.3mn, Fire +23% to Rs.659.0mn, Marine -63% to Rs.13.3mn
Underwriting loss cut 60% to Rs.92.4mn (from Rs.231.9mn): NEP +43% to Rs.3,129.2mn vs operating & admin expenses only +12% to Rs.1,109.5mn
Net claims +49% to Rs.2,050.1mn (65.5% of NEP vs 62.6%); Motor claims +52% to Rs.1,946.5mn (71.8% of Motor NEP vs 68.3%)
Investment & other revenue +12% to Rs.618.0mn (net interest/dividend +7% to Rs.550.5mn, fair-value gains +82% to Rs.66.1mn) exceeds the whole PBT
Rs.2,123.8mn of premium (~41% of GWP) came from customers introduced by parent People's Leasing & Finance; Rs.84.5mn via People's Bank
NAV/share Rs.31.08 vs last price Rs.28.50 (~0.92x book); equity Rs.6,328.8mn; SLFRS 4 under SoAT relief, SLFRS 17 numbers due Q3; unprovided tax assessments Rs.350.9mn
key_drivers: Motor premium growth (+39%, Rs.4,047.2mn) and Miscellaneous premium (+78%) lifted NEP 43%; Motor underwriting margin rose from Rs.531.4mn to Rs.663.5mn
Expense leverage: operating & admin costs +12% vs NEP +43% turned a Rs.231.9mn underwriting loss into Rs.92.4mn
Claims inflation: net claims +49% (Motor +52%), claims paid +84% to Rs.2,960.8mn, took the net claims ratio to 65.5% of NEP from 62.6%
Investment income (Rs.550.5mn net interest/dividends + Rs.66.1mn fair-value gains) funds all of PBT; underwriting remains negative
